bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521507 (glog): Dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_demangle [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521507
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `gt_results/arvo_42521507/_work/src/glog` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 12-byte ASCII witness `_ZZn9ZZZCZAZ` with SHA-256 `51649a8b96c918f84db722d1d5d33f3eb1456aa575058a57d43afe42482d1036` is copied by the fuzz target into stack buffer `Buffer[13]` and passed to `google::Demangle(Buffer, demangled, 12)`. During recursive local-name parsing, `ParseNumber()` consumes bytes `n9` as a `<source-name>` length and stores `length = -9`. Vulnerable `ParseIdentifier()` only rejects `length == -1` or strings shorter than `length`; because `AtLeastNumCharsRemaining(state->mangled_cur, -9)` returns true without iterating, the code accepts `-9` and executes `state->mangled_cur += length`, rewinding the cursor from the first `Z` after `n9` to four bytes before the start of `Buffer`. `ParseUnqualifiedName()` then continues into `Optional(ParseAbiTags(state))`, so `ParseAbiTag()` calls `ParseOneCharToken(state, 'B')` and reads `state->mangled_cur[0]` from the left redzone. AddressSanitizer reports `dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/demangle.cc:211`. The staged patch fixes the witnessed path by rejecting negative identifier lengths before advancing `state->mangled_cur`.

source.description: Source. `ParseNumber()` consumes the attacker-controlled `n` prefix of a `<source-name>` length and turns it into negative-sign state for the parsed length.
source.value_from: The staged 12-byte ASCII `poc` `_ZZn9ZZZCZAZ` with SHA-256 `51649a8b96c918f84db722d1d5d33f3eb1456aa575058a57d43afe42482d1036`. After the parser admits `_Z` and the third-byte local-name marker `Z`, bytes `n9` at offsets 3..4 are presented to `ParseNumber()` as the `<source-name>` length token.
source.note: This is the first project parser statement that converts the input bytes into vulnerability-relevant state. The fuzz target's `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` only stages those bytes in `Buffer` and is the unscored harness boundary.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `ParseIdentifier()` does not reject negative lengths except the special case `-1`, and `AtLeastNumCharsRemaining()` vacuously succeeds for negative `n`, so negative source-name lengths survive validation.
root_cause.note: For the exact witness `length == -9`, so this predicate is false and the function proceeds to `state->mangled_cur += length`. The patch adds an explicit `length < 0` and remaining-length check before that pointer advance.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `ParseOneCharToken()` reads one byte through `state->mangled_cur` after `ParseIdentifier()` has rewound that cursor four bytes before the input stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved stack is `ParseOneCharToken -> ParseAbiTag -> OneOrMore -> ParseAbiTags`, and AddressSanitizer reports `dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line.

parser_admitted.description: The third byte `Z` of the witness enters the recursive local-name production, whose inner `ParseEncoding -> ParseName -> ParseSourceName` path later parses `n9` as the vulnerable negative length.
parser_admitted.note: This is the control checkpoint that admits the staged input to the exact parser path refined below.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment materializes the attacker-controlled length `-9` from bytes `n9` and leaves `state->mangled_cur` at the first `Z` after the number.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Offsets 3..4 of the staged `poc` are ASCII `n9`. `ParseNumber()` consumes `n` as the sign and decimal `9` as the magnitude, then writes the signed result to caller variable `length`.
tainted_value_origin.note: At this point `ParseNumber()` has advanced `state->mangled_cur` from the `9` to `Buffer[5]`, so the later `state->mangled_cur += length` underflow moves relative to that position.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The fuzz target allocates 13-byte stack buffer `Buffer`, copies the 12-byte staged witness `_ZZn9ZZZCZAZ` into `Buffer[0..11]`, and writes `\0` at `Buffer[12]`. All later `state->mangled_cur` reads are intended to stay within this stack extent.

Source step. While parsing the `<source-name>` length inside the admitted `_ZZ...` local-name path, `ParseNumber()` reads byte `n` from the witness and sets `sign = -1`, turning the following decimal digits into a negative length.
The digit loop consumes `9`, stops at the next `Z`, and stores `length = -9` in the caller. `ParseNumber()` also advances `state->mangled_cur` to the first `Z` after `n9`, i.e. `Buffer[5]`.

Root-cause step. With `length == -9`, this guard does not reject the value: only `-1` is special-cased, and `AtLeastNumCharsRemaining(state->mangled_cur, -9)` returns true because its `for (i = 0; i < n; ++i)` loop executes zero iterations for negative `n`.

Because step 4 lets `-9` pass, `ParseIdentifier()` adds that negative length to the current cursor and rewinds `state->mangled_cur` from `Buffer[5]` to `Buffer[-4]`, four bytes before the valid stack buffer from step 1. `ParseSourceName()` still returns true, so later parsing reuses this underflowed cursor.

Sink step. `ParseUnqualifiedName()` immediately evaluates `Optional(ParseAbiTags(state))`, so `ParseAbiTag()` calls `ParseOneCharToken(state, 'B')` on the underflowed cursor from step 5. Reading `state->mangled_cur[0]` at `Buffer[-4]` produces the saved `AddressSanitizer: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this line.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: the saved report is a dynamic stack-buffer-overflow on the fuzz target's VLA input buffer, so there is no separate heap allocation/free context to match.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer stack is `ParseOneCharToken -> ParseAbiTag -> OneOrMore -> ParseAbiTags -> ParseUnqualifiedName -> ParseUnscopedName -> ParseUnscopedTemplateName -> ParseName -> ParseEncoding -> ParseLocalName -> ParseName -> ParseEncoding -> ParseMangledName -> ParseTopLevelMangledName -> Demangle -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and the fine trace refines the same project path with the earlier `ParseNumber` and `ParseIdentifier` steps that have already returned by the time frame 0 faults.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42521507 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/fuzz_demangle` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` with stack `ParseOneCharToken -> ParseAbiTag -> OneOrMore`.

format.name: glog demangle ASCII witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 12-byte ASCII file `_ZZn9ZZZCZAZ` with SHA-256 `51649a8b96c918f84db722d1d5d33f3eb1456aa575058a57d43afe42482d1036`. The fuzz target copies those 12 bytes into `Buffer[13]`, appends `\0`, and calls `google::Demangle(Buffer, demangled, 12)`. On this exact witness the leading `_ZZ` admits the local-name parse, bytes `n9` are materialized as `length = -9`, and `ParseIdentifier()` rewinds `state->mangled_cur` from `Buffer[5]` to `Buffer[-4]`; `ParseAbiTag()` then tests for `'B'` by reading `state->mangled_cur[0]`, causing the saved out-of-bounds read. Stage 01 proves only this exact witness and observed parser path; this contract does not generalize to other mangled names or neighboring negative lengths.
